title: Lynx Analytics outreach - WIP
body:
Quick brain dump and working playbook for Lynx Analytics outreach

1) Quick account signal summary
- Company: Lynx Analytics (mid-market analytics platform focused on retail intelligence)
- HQ: Chicago, ~220 employees, recently raised Series B H2 2024
- Tech: Python stack, heavy use of Snowflake and dbt, serving analytics forecasts to B2B customers. Recent job posts for ML infra and SRE.
- Likely drivers: reduce inference cost for batch scoring, embed fast explanations in dashboards, tighten latency for near-realtime insights at scale
- Compliance: processes for SOC2 in progress; some customers require data residency and contractual controls

2) Why Redwood could matter to them (value hooks)
- Cost: intelligent batching and KV caching reduces token spend on repeat prompts for dashboard refreshes
- Latency: dedicated capacity or private deployment for predictable 200-400ms token latencies on typical forecast prompts
- Deployment modes: option to start hosted API for POC then migrate to private VPC for enterprise customers with residency needs
- Observability: route-level latency and token cost breakdowns map directly to their CFO metric asks

3) Primary stakeholders to target (hypothesis)
- Head of ML / Director of ML Engineering (likely champion)
- Platform lead or infra manager (evaluates infra ops and SLAs)
- Product lead for Embedded Analytics (buyer for end-user features)
- Security/compliance manager (required for private deployment conversations)

4) Initial outreach sequence (multi-channel)
- Touch 1: Short cold email from me (Evelyn) to Head of ML. Subject lines to test:
  - "Reduce inference cost for Lynx forecast pipelines"
  - "Fast, predictable LLM inference for embedded retail insights"
  Body: 2 short paragraphs, callout of 1 concrete idea (KV caching to cut repeated prompt cost by 30%), ask for 20 min intro

- Touch 2: LinkedIn connection + one-liner referencing email, attach 1-pager PDF (light)

- Touch 3: Follow-up email with a quick case study (anonymized) highlighting a 40% cost reduction and stable SLOs for a similar analytics customer

- Touch 4: If no response, reach out to platform lead with technical probing question about current batch scoring cadence and peak QPS

5) Call agenda template (20 minutes)
- 0-3m: intros and context - confirm current stack and top latency/cost pain
- 3-8m: quick sketch of how Redwood fits into their top flows (hosted -> dedicated -> private path)
- 8-14m: metrics and examples - token cost per dashboard refresh, expected throughput, SLA needs
- 14-18m: security/compliance checklist - data residency, KMS, audit logs
- 18-20m: agree next steps - POC scope, data access, point people, timeline

6) Tech fit notes to capture during discovery
- typical sequence length for prompts (tokens), avg tokens per dashboard call
- concurrent QPS at peak and average
- cacheability of prompts: how many prompts are repeated across users/dashboards
- whether LLM runs in a VPC or can it call into Snowflake via external function (we may need private connector)
- acceptance criteria for POC: latency threshold, inference cost target, quality/regression tolerance

7) Objections and quick counters (playbook style)
- Objection: "We already use cheap open weights on our own infra"
  Counter: Redwood focuses on serving optimizations and routing plus an orchestration layer. For the same or lower unit cost we provide predictable latency, autoscaling, and fallback policies that reduce engineering maintenance overhead
- Objection: "Security and data residency is non-negotiable"
  Counter: Offer private deployment plan overview, KMS integration, audit logs, and reference to SOC2 roadmap. Propose an architecture sketch for air-gapped or VPC-hosted control plane
- Objection: "We can't add another PR to our infra backlog"
  Counter: Start with hosted POC for quick wins, or Dedicated with turnkey support from our solutions engineering team. We can demo integration in 2 weeks with minimal infra changes
- Objection: "Cost seems unclear"
  Counter: Provide modeled estimate based on their token distribution; propose a 3-week POC with cost and latency reporting and a cap to limit surprise spend

8) Email drafts (shortened, to iterate)
- Cold email version A:
  Subject: Reduce inference spend for Lynx forecast pipelines
  Hi NAME,

  Quick note — we help data-driven platforms reduce per-call LLM spend and keep token latency predictable as usage scales. For teams like yours we often see 25-50% lower unit cost with caching and workload-aware batching while keeping output quality the same.

  If interested I can share a short cost model specific to Lynx and a 2-week POC plan. 20 minutes next week?

  Best,
  Evelyn

- Cold email version B (technical):
  Subject: baseline QPS + caching idea for Lynx dashboards
  Hi NAME,

  Saw your open ML infra roles and wanted to see if you have a few minutes to talk about a quick idea: prefix/KV caching that reuses expensive prompt context across dashboard refreshes. For a partner last quarter this cut token usage by ~30% and reduced p99 latency variance.

  Would love 20 minutes to sketch how it might map to your flows.
  Evelyn

9) POC proposal skeleton (for when we get interest)
- Duration: 3 weeks (pilot)
- Scope: instrument 3 key dashboard endpoints for inference, collect token profiles, enable caching, run on Redwood hosted or dedicated depending on security need
- Success metrics: 30% token cost reduction target or p99 latency under agreed threshold, no quality regressions on sample prompt set
- Delivery: solutions eng + one platform contact from Lynx

10) Next steps and owners
- Send first cold email by EOD Monday - owner: Evelyn
- Prep 1-pager and anonymized case study - owner: Lina (due 2025-01-20)
- Schedule internal sync with solutions engineering to prep POC kit - owner: Ravi (due 2025-01-22)
- If no reply after 10 days, escalate to platform lead contact via mutual intro - owner: Evelyn

11) Notes to self / todo items
- Confirm whether Lynx uses private Snowflake accounts per customer (this affects connector approach)
- Draft a quick network diagram for private deployment options to drop into next email
- Gather anonymized cost model from last retail analytics POC to reference
- Run subject-line A/B for first 50 recipients in sequence

End of scratchpad. Keep light and iterative. This is intentionally messy — update after discovery call.
